excerpt: When I see a large assignment I start by checking emails because that feels manageable, even though I know it is not the priority.
I usually wait until the lecturer gives an example. Until then I worry I will misunderstand the question.
I open the document early but sometimes stare at it for an hour because writing the first sentence feels like committing to an answer.
Deadlines help me. If there are smaller checkpoints I tend to work steadily, but with one final date I convince myself there is still plenty of time.
Paid work comes first some weeks. I would not call that procrastination because I am choosing rent over an essay.
I avoid assignments most when I care about them. If I think I might do badly, doing nothing protects me from finding out.
Clear rubrics make a big difference. I can turn criteria into a checklist and start with one item.
Sometimes I delay deliberately because I know I need time to think. Starting immediately is not always better for me.
I get distracted by useful tasks like cleaning or organising notes. They give me a sense that I have achieved something.
When feedback tells me exactly what to change I can move quickly. General comments like 'develop this' make me freeze.
My caring responsibilities are unpredictable, so the timetable other students use does not always fit my week.
I often think I need to feel motivated before I begin, but once I do five minutes the motivation usually follows.
If I have already had a bad grade in a subject, the next assignment feels threatening before I even read it.
I work best with another person nearby. It is not that they help with the work, it just makes leaving the task harder.
Sometimes I submit close to the deadline because I keep improving things. The delay is not always avoidance.
A vague title makes me search for more and more sources because I am afraid I have missed the right interpretation.
When lecturers release all deadlines at once I can plan. When dates change, I lose trust in my schedule and postpone.
I know exactly what to do but still choose games because the reward is immediate and the essay reward feels far away.
